background: Raiffeisen Bank International is the central institution of the Austrian Raiffeisen cooperative banks and a leading lender across Central and Eastern Europe, with a large and long-running exposure to Russia that it has been unable to fully exit.
synthesis: Raiffeisen Bank International is rated A on average across two of the three main agencies, the weakest of them at A-, one on a positive outlook and one on a stable outlook; the last move was a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 11 Jul 2023. Capital is strong, with CET1 of 18.3% and leverage of 8.8% both in the top quarter of EU and Nordic banks, as is NSFR of 155%, but LCR of 144% is now below the median after falling 38 points since 30 Jun 2025. Over the same period leverage has risen 0.5 points and NSFR 11 points, with CET1 broadly flat (figures to 30 Jun 2026). The flagged news centres on sanctions, with allegations weighing on the name and the newest item, on 22 Sep 2026, a default judgment won against Rasperia.
